title: Nvidia Negotiates $25B Reflection AI Deal to Avoid Antitrust
summary:
The computing giant is exploring an 'acqui-hire' transaction with Reflection AI to absorb its employees and technology while sidestepping a full merger review, according to the Financial Times. Nvidia is in early talks to either purchase the American open-weight model startup, which is valued at $25 billion, or increase its current equity stake. A deal could be reached within weeks, though the negotiations remain in an early stage and could still fail.

Reflection AI, founded by former Google DeepMind researchers, launched its first open-weight model "Beam" on Monday to compete with Chinese rivals like GLM-5.2. Nvidia has already invested $800 million in the startup, and observers note the acquisition would help the chipmaker drive GPU demand as open-weight models surged to 78.4% of token volume on one major AI gateway by September. This strategy may also aim to improve the performance of Nvidia's own Nemotron models.

selectedTweets.text:
According to the Financial Times, Nvidia is in talks to acquire Reflection AI, the American open weight model startup it has already put $800 million into.

Reflection AI was founded in 2024 by former Google DeepMind researchers and on Monday it launched its first open weight model, called Beam, to compete in coding and agentic tasks. This chart explains why Nvidia cares so much. On one major AI gateway, open weight models went from a minority of token volume in June to 78.4% by mid-September while closed models are down to just 21.6%. Closed models like Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.6 Sol still take the biggest share of the dollars, but Chinese open models like Kimi K3 and DeepSeek are already in the top 10.

That is the problem for the United States. Most of the best open weight models today come from China and Reflection is one of the few serious American companies trying to change that. For Nvidia, every open model that gets downloaded and deployed still needs GPUs to run. If the leading American open models are built and optimized on Nvidia hardware, that drives even more demand for $NVDA https://t.co/eR4mQAX7xG also moves Nvidia closer to owning the full stack.

Jensen is once again playing 4D chess.
selectedTweets.quotedTweetText:
Cheaper tokens do not mean less compute, they mean more of it.

@GavinSBaker is exactly right here because an open weight token uses roughly the same compute and energy as a closed model token when the models are a similar size.This chart from one AI gateway shows how fast the shift is happening. Open weight models were a minority of token volume in June, and by mid-September they made up 78.4% of it. While the spend data tells a very different story. Closed models like Claude Opus 4.8 and GPT 5.6 Sol still take the biggest share of the dollars, even though they are losing share of the tokens. That gap is the whole point. Developers are moving their volume to cheaper models, but they are not using less AI because of it but using a lot more.

Ramp's data in Gavin's chart shows the same pattern. Token volumes rose about 7x from January to September, while AI spend actually fell over the same period. This means the model layer is likely to see its margins squeezed as prices keep falling. Gavin also points out that open weight tokens are some of the highest margin tokens for the cloud providers that serve them. Every one of those tokens still has to run on GPUs, memory and networking gear. Cheaper models make AI more affordable, and that pulls even more demand into the data center.

That is why I think the infrastructure layer keeps winning no matter which model wins. The companies I am watching most closely are $NVDA, $AMD, $AVGO and $MU. Bullish on AI infrastructure.
